recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future Condition.category work should follow newer category trackers rather than re-opening this duplicate DSTU2 boundary comment.
issue_request: FHIR-11211 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU2 Patient Care ballot issue asking to clarify the boundary between Observation and Condition because old Condition.category codes such as finding and symptom appeared to conflict with boundary guidance.
initial_application: The substantive boundary clarification was applied through the original FHIR-8872 implementation commit f5f5c6ecae. The category-code part of the concern was addressed by bffc717a99, which replaced the old complaint/symptom/finding/diagnosis category set with problem-list-item and encounter-diagnosis as part of the FHIR-10091/10404 category work.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini. Current Condition boundary text preserves the FHIR-8872 rule and later refinements, while Observation cross-references the same boundary and acknowledges selected overlap. Later Condition.category decisions, including FHIR-48358 and FHIR-54454, made the binding example-strength and removed the misleading code-list short display.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current spec already gives the requested guidance and no current core source lists symptom or finding as Condition.category codes.
